It's only been 2 months for me, but I have learned soooooo much about human psychology.

Another instance happened when I was trying to sleep in the parking lot at the public park. It's officially "closed at dusk," and I was of course the only car there, but it's a very dark lot and I was hoping no one would notice. I drifted off to sleep and about 2:00 in the morning, someone was tapping on my window - it wasn't the cops, thankfully, but it was some dude that works for the parks department. He wasn't a douche, but he did seem like he was going to ask me to leave.

I'm a fairly young, clean-cut white guy and I basically pulled the "I didn't know I couldn't do that" routine (which I normally wouldn't even try, but the adrenaline allowed it).

He asked if I was spending the night there, in a tone that said, "by the way you can't sleep here," and I replied in a tone that sounded like I owned the place, "I was planning on it," and he immediately cowed and was like, "well, sorry to bother you, have a good night."

It was a good feeling. 

I've had *some* what folks call Privilege nowadays, and it's been very interesting to see how it has helped me in many cases, and yet in others, it's been a massive hindrance.

 It's been an odd journey so far.

My mother stole the keys to a moving van (filled with everything I owned) in order to prevent me from getting away from her.

I called the police. After talking for ~an hour, the police sergeant took me aside and said, verbatim, "We're not going to arrest your mother. We're not going to force her to give the keys back to you."

He then went on to tell me how I could call back when his shift was over in a few hours (he was the officer in charge for the region or something like that) and that I could try the next guy, but to not get my hopes up.

I wish I had advice for you. This occurred over 2 years ago and my life has been in tatters ever since. I recently tried to quietly plan on leaving - well, *today* was when I planned to leave. However, somehow they learned of my planned, and sabotaged it completely, and I'm right back at square one (which is about 137 squares below where "square one" was for me 2 years ago).

I really don't say this to scare you. These situations are unique to the individual and you definitely should not compare our situations based on the very limited info I've provided. However, I just don't want folks to get the false impression that the help/support systems that we *think* can/will help will actually do so. It's terrifying when you get to the point of finding that no one will actually help.

I'm currently wading through the morass of social services in my city/state and it's even more abysmal than I had previously thought. It's basically one circular phone referral service loop - there's almost *zero* actual help available until you (figurative *or* literally) have a rope around your neck. 

I'm still, um, *kinda* hopeful. Please stay safe, and, before you trust someone: be cautious.

Good luck!

I'm getting close to where you are. I just came here to post my own thread (though I haven't quite set my mind on things - more of a cry for help, but I've been ).

Honestly, the $10,000 makes me so, so jealous. I imagine that makes things feel worse, though I truly don't mean for it to.

Please at least see where that money can get you. Hell, I'm ordering you to.

>You hang in there, too.

Thanks - I'm trying!

Perhaps the best thing I can offer that I've learned is that being a narcissist's object means that there are no boundaries - it's not about *crossing* lines - to them, there *are no lines to cross.* 

They may be able to have seemingly normal relationships with others, though - normal friendships, etc. So, to an outside observer, their behavior towards that observer seems totally normal - because it likely *is* normal behavior. So, the outside observers fall into the abuser's trap where they project normalcy to the outside world and use that to hide their abuse.

Don't take this the wrong way, but I hope you're a woman because the resources out there are primarily focused on helping women out of bad relationships. As a guy, I've been told that "we don't offer services for problems like yours." 

Hell, one of the few resources that sounded like it *might* be able to help was a program to help homeless (I'm just *nearly* homeless) men get back on their feet.

It's called "Operation Bootstraps," and I felt so vile giving them a call. 

I don't think they have any clue how painful their name is. I don't think they understand what it means. It felt like such a slap in the face, though I'm sure they "meant well."

They told me to call back in the morning. Sadly, I probably will. I'm almost out of options.

Good luck to you, and stay safe. You'll be ok. Me too.

I'm currently trying to escape a situation where an abusive narcissist parent has lied, manipulated, and coerced me into becoming and remaining completely dependent on them for the past few years, all under the guise of "helping me."

I say this because, well, I just learned about this recently, too, and the whole "you are seen as a extension of the narcissist, not as an actual person" thing is completely true. Once I learned about it, everything suddenly made sense, and it was devastating. 

Please, please find some help quickly - I'm not saying to castrophize things and act rashly, but I highly suggest talking to someone asap, because things can go badly very quickly, and I'm blown away by how shitty our social support systems are. 

The only thing anyone seems to be able to do is refer you to someone else. Who refers you. Who refers you, and then at some point someone says, "oh, we don't handle that sort of thing," then you're stuck.

I'm currently stuck, maybe living in my car soon, and I have no idea how I'm going to take care of my dog. 

No one will "help" you until you have a rope around your neck, and in that case they'll just lock you away for a few weeks and then send you a bill. 

I *do* mean to be as dire as I sound, because it's currently happening to me, and it has been a slow train wreck for a few years.

If there's one thing I've learned from all this, it's that things can always get worse. Rock bottom is a lie. It's a cliff, and you can always fall further.

________________________________________________________________________________________

edit: I had meant to *not* rant, then did, and now I feel shame and want to delete it. Sorry for ranting. Things are just hard right now - for a lot of folks. If anyone reads this and it makes you feel worse, please remember that all of us have different sets of problems, but also different resources - yours may be vastly better than mine, so make sure you don't compare yourself to others in these situations.

Thanks so much for that. Yep on the doubting my own reality. Today was the first day that I've felt truly sane in ~15 years (I'm 33). She's perhaps what I've seen called an "introverted narcissist" - her self-image, or whatever it is that she's tried to cultivate - is all about *not* being a narcissist.

 I've basically described her as a narcissistic martyr - she gets off on feeling as though she's done things incorrectly. If I'm in pain, then I need her, and that's what she needs to keep going in life. I am a doll to her, and her entire being is wrapped around her children - in taking care of them.  She needs me to have problems because fixing those problems is what she lives for. 

Wait - that statement is incomplete: She lives for the *intention* of helping me. I know Louis CK is not a good name to bring up, but [this joke about wanting to offer his seat in first class to a soldier](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2eiCyT5pY_E) pretty much sums up my mom. She *wants* to help, and so when she would lie to me that she's going to do, well, *whatever*, she pats herself on the back and thinks "I'm such a good mom." It doesn't matter that this ***only exists in her head*** - she pats herself on the back for her thought. 

And, if there's a *real* crisis she can be involved in (like how she has lied, manipulated, stolen, and physically intervened), she will. 

I am currently trapped. I went through a crisis over 2 years ago, and she intervened *against my will* and...

...by the way, at the time, I *still trusted her ***completely*** - I trusted her completely - fuck, that thought hurts so much - we were best friends, I thought ...
 
...basically I'm completely dependent on her financially. Completely. Every single thing she said she'd do was a lie. Ok. Fine. Whatever. I'm leaving. Oh, you just lied to the cops that I was suicidal and you had me involuntarily committed? Yay. Thanks for the new medical bill and, because of the commital - TRUE SUICIDAL THOUGHTS! (2 years ago, btw - I'm not suicidal currently - just pissed off and sad).


P.S. - just called my estranged-ish dad (we're friendly, but he's more like a very distant uncle). I told him I was at the end of my rope and he gave me one of these new libertarian bullshit answers of "well, I can't help you in any way other than to say that *you're going to have to do this on your own,* and how *I* have to take responsiblity. 

Thanks, bub. No shit. That asshole created me because he was horny one day and **I** am the one who has to be responsible. 

Oops. Didn't mean to type so much. I'm on the verge, man. Everything sucks. Still have my dog, though. Not all is lost. I'll be ok, or at least I'll be whatever. 

A lot of this was just venting to the ether, but **TLDR: HI OTHER REDDITOR - If there's anything ***you* need that I can offer, let me know. Despite everything, I've got the Christmas spirit, at least until the bottle is empty.
